title: Why Talking to Friends Can Actually Reduce Physical Pain
hook: Feeling pain? Your social life might be the secret remedy.

narration.text: Feeling pain? Your social life might be the secret remedy.
When we connect with others, our brains release a hormone called oxytocin.
Oxytocin is often called the 'love hormone', but it does much more.
It plays a key role in social bonding, trust, and empathy.
This hormone can also act as a natural painkiller.
It helps to calm the nervous system and reduce our perception of discomfort.
So, connecting with friends isn't just good for your mood, it's good for your body too.
Have you noticed socialising helping with minor aches or stresses?

description: Discover the surprising link between social interaction and pain relief. Learn how oxytocin, often called the 'love hormone', can naturally reduce physical discomfort by calming your nervous system. Prioritise your social connections for better well-being.
topic: Why social interaction can reduce feelings of pain, explaining the role of oxytocin.
